Messages.Author: Gary Schwartz
Messages.Body:
1) Two vampires are in combat, both with superior Thaumaturgy. One has
1 blood and the other 2 when strikes are chosen. Both play Theft of Vitae as
the strike. How many blood does each vampire have after strike resolution?

2) It says in the rulebook "if a combat card does not state that it can
be used at long range then the card can only be used at close range."
This has got to be wrong since otherwise no damage could be prevented
at long range, and things like combat ends & dodge could not be used
at long range. On the other hand, if you can dodges & combat ends, etc.
at long range, then what about the Quietus strike "Weakness"?

Thanks,
Gary S.

Messages.Author: Alec Chang
Messages.Body:
In article <4rtld6$4...@vixen.cso.uiuc.edu>, schw...@math.uiuc.edu
says...

1)They switch blood, since their strikes are resolved simultaneously, and
they can't steal more blood than the other vampire has.

2)Strikes, except strike:dodges and Strike:Combat ends, are not sucessful
at long range unless they are specifically listed as ranged on the card.
I think that there aren't any exceptions to that one.

Alec Chang

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
schw...@math.uiuc.edu (Gary Schwartz) writes:

>1) Two vampires are in combat, both with superior Thaumaturgy. One has
>1 blood and the other 2 when strikes are chosen. Both play Theft of Vitae as
>the strike. How many blood does each vampire have after strike resolution?

Both strikes are applies simultaneously, so the first steals all (2) from
the second, while the second steals all (1) from the first. The first
ends with two, the second ends with one.

>2) It says in the rulebook "if a combat card does not state that it can
>be used at long range then the card can only be used at close range."
>This has got to be wrong since otherwise no damage could be prevented
>at long range, and things like combat ends & dodge could not be used
>at long range. On the other hand, if you can dodges & combat ends, etc.
>at long range, then what about the Quietus strike "Weakness"?

It refers only to strikes, correct. All other combat cards apply
at either range, unless restricted by card text, of course. (Anything
that deals damage during strike resolution obeys the same guidelines,
though, like Wolf Companion et. al.)

Messages.Author: David Pontes
Messages.Body:
On 9 Jul 1996, Gary Schwartz wrote:

> 1) Two vampires are in combat, both with superior Thaumaturgy. One has
> 1 blood and the other 2 when strikes are chosen. Both play Theft of Vitae as
> the strike. How many blood does each vampire have after strike resolution?

I heard that "the stolen blood can be used to prevent damage",
but since steal blood does no damage, the blood actually 'arrives' at the
end of damage resolution, I guess.
So, #1 setals #2's blood, and vice-versa. What happens is that
they 'trade blood' :)

>
> 2) It says in the rulebook "if a combat card does not state that it can
> be used at long range then the card can only be used at close range."
> This has got to be wrong since otherwise no damage could be prevented
> at long range, and things like combat ends & dodge could not be used
> at long range. On the other hand, if you can dodges & combat ends, etc.
> at long range, then what about the Quietus strike "Weakness"?
>

I believe that this phrase was only meant for strike cards, not
damage prevention.
As for Dodge and CE, they are still legal to play at long range
because of their definition: "Dodge prevents the effect of the opponent's
strike" (this may even include steal blood, I believe), and CE "ends the
combat".

One way to properly say this would be "any strike that does not
mention range can only affect your opponent at short range". Since Dodge
and SCE does not affect your opponent (only what your opponent does to you),
this might be better. Of course, Riposte comes to mind, and there goes my
theory :)

David Pontes
